newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound firms, eyes on Brown/George meeting.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound firms, eyes on Brown/George meeting.

text.p: The Irish pound gained ground against both sterling and the mark in early trade on Tuesday but dealers said activity was light and attention was focused on the Brown/George meeting in the UK.
Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown brought forward his monthly monetary meeting with Bank of England governor Eddie George to today.
Brown is widely expected to raise Britain's six percent base rate by a quarter of a point.
"Sterling is fairly subdued. People are waiting on news from the Brown/George meeting at 1100 (1000 GMT) and until then things will be fairly quiet," one dealer said.
By 0830 GMT, the Irish pound was at 0.9260 marks, down from an earlier high of 0.9285 marks but above last Friday's close of 0.9245. It edged up to 2.5925 marks from 2.5835 on Friday.
"There seems to be some demand this morning. The market is still very short of Irish pounds so you are probably seeing some profit-taking," one dealer said.
But he added that sellers of mark/Irish were likely to emerge above 2.60 marks.
On the money markets, Irish interbank rates eased slightly, with the one-month rate slipping back to 6.12/6.25 from 6.31/6.43 late on Friday.
As yet, none of Ireland's financial institutions have increased rates following the Irish Central Bank's decision to raise official rates by 50 basis points last Thursday.

But newspaper reports said that Irish Permanent, which has already withdrawn its range of fixed rate mortgage options for new borrowers, is expected to kick off a round of rate rises today with an increase of 50 basis points in its rates.
